literal: unfortunately · and · words · hit the mark

meaning.en: A gloomy prediction made in passing has, unluckily, turned out to be right.
meaning.zh: 不希望发生的事，被自己说中了。

equivalents: I wish I hadn't been right
a prophecy that came true, sadly

examples.zh: 他早说公司会倒闭，没想到不幸而言中。
examples.en: He had said the firm would go under, and sadly he was proved right.

examples.zh: 天气预报说周末有暴雨，不幸而言中，活动只好取消。
examples.en: The forecast warned of a downpour at the weekend, and unluckily it was right, so the event was cancelled.

examples.zh: 我担心他会迟到，不幸而言中，他果然误了航班。
examples.en: I worried he would be late, and my fear came true: he missed his flight.

usage.en: Predicate, often as a comment after the event; wry or regretful tone.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用于事后感叹，带无奈、惋惜的语气。

natural: say this, that and the other

meaning.en: To talk at great length, giving every kind of reason; often 'whatever you say, in the end…'.
meaning.zh: 说了很多话，讲了各种理由；常引出“总之、归根结底”的结论。

examples.zh: 说千道万，最关键的还是要自己努力。
examples.en: Whatever else you say, what matters most is making an effort yourself.

examples.zh: 他说千道万，就是不肯承认自己错了。
examples.en: He talked and talked, but would not admit he was wrong.

examples.zh: 不管你怎么说千道万，我都不会改变主意。
examples.en: No matter how much you say, I won't change my mind.

usage.en: Predicate or sentence opener; colloquial.
usage.zh: 作谓语或句首插入语，口语色彩。

meaning.en: Acts of rape, looting and plunder, typically by invading soldiers or bandits.
meaning.zh: 指强奸妇女、抢劫财物等暴行。

examples.zh: 侵略军所到之处，奸淫掳掠，无恶不作。
examples.en: Wherever the invaders went they raped and plundered, committing every crime.

examples.zh: 这伙土匪烧杀抢掠，奸淫掳掠，百姓苦不堪言。
examples.en: The bandits burned, killed, raped and looted, and the people suffered unspeakably.

examples.zh: 历史书记载了军阀部队奸淫掳掠的罪行。
examples.en: History books record the crimes of rape and plunder by warlord troops.

usage.en: Predicate or object; grave, formal, used for atrocities in war or banditry.
usage.zh: 作谓语或宾语；语气严厉，多用于战乱、匪患中的暴行。

meaning.en: Having no fixed position: either way is fine; also a lukewarm, indifferent attitude.
meaning.zh: 没有固定的主张，怎样都行；也指态度无所谓。

examples.zh: 对于吃什么，他无可无不可，一切听你的。
examples.en: As to what to eat, he has no preference and leaves it all to you.

examples.zh: 她对这桩婚事抱着无可无不可的态度。
examples.en: She took an indifferent, either-way attitude to the marriage.

examples.zh: 做人不能事事无可无不可，该坚持的要坚持。
examples.en: One cannot be so easygoing about everything; some things must be insisted on.

story.en: Confucius contrasts himself with other worthies: 'I am different from these: there is nothing I insist on and nothing I rule out' (我则异于是，无可无不可).
story.zh: 《论语·微子》：“我则异于是，无可无不可。”孔子自言没有固定的可与不可，视情况而定。

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; neutral to slightly critical when it means indifference.
usage.zh: 作谓语或定语；表示不拘泥时为中性，表示漠不关心时略带贬义。

pinyin: yǐ gǔ wéi jìng, kě yǐ zhī xīng tì
literal: take · the past · as · mirror · can · thereby · know · rise · fall
natural: history is a mirror of rise and fall

meaning.en: Study history as a mirror, and you can understand why states and dynasties rise and fall.
meaning.zh: 以历史为镜子，可以明白国家兴衰更替的道理。

examples.zh: 以古为镜，可以知兴替，读史能帮助我们看清今天。
examples.en: Take the past as a mirror to know why states rise and fall: reading history helps us see today clearly.

examples.zh: 老师引用“以古为镜，可以知兴替”，鼓励大家多读历史。
examples.en: The teacher quoted 'take the past as a mirror to know rise and fall' to encourage us to read more history.

examples.zh: 以古为镜，可以知兴替，决策者更应当熟知历史教训。
examples.en: Decision-makers above all should know the lessons of history.

story.en: Wei Zheng died in 643; Emperor Taizong said: 'With bronze as a mirror one can straighten one's cap; with the past as a mirror one can know rise and fall; with people as a mirror one can see gains and losses.'
story.zh: 魏徵去世后，唐太宗说：“夫以铜为镜，可以正衣冠；以古为镜，可以知兴替；以人为镜，可以明得失。”

usage.en: A quotation, usually cited whole or as the first clause of a triplet (铜镜 / 古镜 / 人镜).
usage.zh: 名言，常整句引用，也常与“以铜为镜”“以人为镜”连用。

literal: the character 八 · not yet · one · left stroke
natural: not even the first stroke written

meaning.en: Barely begun; nothing is settled yet.
meaning.zh: 事情还没有眼目，还远没有成功或确定。

examples.zh: 别高兴得太早，这事八字没一撇呢。
examples.en: Don't celebrate too soon; the deal is nowhere near settled.

examples.zh: 他们打算开公司，可是八字没一撇，连资金都没落实。
examples.en: They plan to start a company, but it's barely begun and they haven't even secured funding.

examples.zh: 你们还没领证，婚礼的事八字没一撇。
examples.en: You haven't even registered, so the wedding is a long way from settled.

usage.en: Predicate, colloquial; often also 还没有八字一撇 (some say 一撇都没有).
usage.zh: 作谓语，口语；常说“还没影儿”“八字还没一撇”。

literal: full · warm · think of · lust · desire
natural: once well fed and warm, thoughts turn to vice

meaning.en: People who have enough to eat and wear tend to turn to self-indulgence.
meaning.zh: 人吃饱穿暖之后，就容易产生放纵享乐的念头。

examples.zh: 古人说“饱暖思淫欲”，生活富足后更要自律。
examples.en: The ancients said that comfort breeds vice, so once life is easy we need more self-discipline.

examples.zh: 他暴富后沉迷声色，真是饱暖思淫欲。
examples.en: After getting rich he sank into dissipation: comfort truly breeds vice.

examples.zh: 饱暖思淫欲，饥寒起盗心，这句老话道出了人性的弱点。
examples.en: 'Comfort breeds vice, hunger breeds theft': this old saying names a weakness of human nature.

usage.en: Proverb, usually paired with 饥寒起盗心; critical, often as a sigh.
usage.zh: 谚语，常与“饥寒起盗心”连用；带批评或感叹意味。

literal: not · worth · one · smile of scorn

meaning.en: So worthless that it does not even deserve a scornful smile.
meaning.zh: 不值得一笑，形容毫无价值，不屑一提。

examples.zh: 这种无稽之谈，不值一哂。
examples.en: Such nonsense is not worth a smirk.

examples.zh: 在大师面前，我的这点本事不值一哂。
examples.en: Next to a master, my modest skill is not worth a smile.

examples.zh: 他的指责不值一哂，我们不必理会。
examples.en: His accusations are beneath contempt and we needn't respond.

usage.en: Predicate; literary, either scornful or self-deprecating.
usage.zh: 作谓语；书面语，可表示轻蔑，也可作自谦。

meaning.en: A business with little capital and thin profit margins.
meaning.zh: 本钱小，利润也薄，多指小买卖。

examples.zh: 小店本小利薄，实在经不起涨价。
examples.en: The little shop runs on small capital and thin margins and can't afford a price rise.

examples.zh: 本小利薄的生意，全靠薄利多销。
examples.en: A business with such thin margins lives on high volume.

examples.zh: 摊主说本小利薄，不能再讲价了。
examples.en: The stallholder said his margins were too slim for more haggling.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; often a seller's plea in bargaining.
usage.zh: 作谓语或定语；买卖中常作卖方自白。

meaning.en: Wind and clouds change colour: a sudden turn in the situation, or great upheaval.
meaning.zh: 风云改变颜色，比喻局势发生剧烈变化，或战争、动乱带来巨大震动。

equivalents: the situation takes a dramatic turn

examples.zh: 这一事件让国际局势为之风云变色。
examples.en: The incident sent the international situation into turmoil.

examples.zh: 暴雨前夕，天空风云变色。
examples.en: Before the downpour, the sky darkened and the clouds churned.

examples.zh: 金融危机来袭，市场一时风云变色。
examples.en: When the financial crisis struck, the market suddenly turned stormy.

usage.en: Predicate; literal for weather, figurative for politics and markets; often 为之风云变色.
usage.zh: 作谓语；本指天气，多比喻政治、市场等的剧变，常说“为之风云变色”。

pinyin: yī wù bù zhī, rú zhě zhī chǐ
literal: one · thing · not · know · Confucian scholar · 's · shame
natural: a scholar should be ashamed of knowing nothing of any one thing

meaning.en: A true scholar should be ashamed to be ignorant of even one thing.
meaning.zh: 读书人若有一样事物不知道，就是耻辱，勉人博学。

equivalents: ignorance of one thing shames a scholar

examples.zh: “一物不知，儒者之耻”，他读书从不放过任何细节。
examples.en: 'Not knowing one thing is a scholar's shame': he never lets a detail slip when he reads.

examples.zh: 老教授常说一物不知，儒者之耻，劝我们多涉猎。
examples.en: The old professor often said that a scholar is shamed by ignorance of even one thing, urging us to read widely.

examples.zh: 一物不知，儒者之耻，可知识总有边界。
examples.en: 'Not knowing one thing is a scholar's shame', yet knowledge always has limits.

usage.en: Saying, often quoted to urge broad learning; slightly ironic when used of oneself.
usage.zh: 谚语式的名言，勉励博学；用于自己时略带自嘲。

meaning.en: Having become even more intense, widespread or serious today than before.
meaning.zh: 到现在更加厉害，多指不良现象愈演愈烈。

examples.zh: 网络诈骗于今为烈，大家要提高警惕。
examples.en: Online fraud is worse than ever now, so everyone must stay alert.

examples.zh: 环境污染问题于今为烈。
examples.en: Environmental pollution has become more serious than ever.

examples.zh: 这种歪风古已有之，于今为烈。
examples.en: This bad habit is old, but it is at its worst today.

usage.en: Predicate; formal, nearly always about undesirable phenomena.
usage.zh: 作谓语；书面语，几乎都指不良现象。

natural: no room to get a word in

meaning.en: Having no opening or standing to put in a word.
meaning.zh: 没有插嘴发表意见的余地。

equivalents: unable to get a word in

examples.zh: 他们争论的是专业问题，外行人无从置喙。
examples.en: They are arguing about technical questions on which a layman has no say.

examples.zh: 这是人家的家事，我无从置喙。
examples.en: This is their family matter, and I have no standing to comment.

examples.zh: 对方说得头头是道，我一时无从置喙。
examples.en: He spoke so persuasively that I couldn't find anything to say.

usage.en: Predicate; formal. Often 不容置喙 means 'allowing no comment'.
usage.zh: 作谓语；书面语。“不容置喙”指不允许别人插嘴。

pinyin: zhì zhī sǐ dì ér hòu kuài
literal: put · him · to · death · place · and · only then · satisfied
natural: not content till he is dead

meaning.en: To hate someone so much that one is not satisfied until he is destroyed.
meaning.zh: 非把对方弄死才称心，形容极端仇恨。

equivalents: not satisfied until he is finished

examples.zh: 他对旧日对手恨之入骨，非要置之死地而后快。
examples.en: He hated his old rival to the bone and would not rest until he was destroyed.

examples.zh: 有人想置之死地而后快，不择手段地诽谤他。
examples.en: Some wanted him ruined and slandered him by any means.

examples.zh: 商场竞争再激烈，也不应置之死地而后快。
examples.en: However fierce business competition is, it should not aim at destroying the other side.

usage.en: Predicate; strongly negative. Do not confuse with 置之死地而后生 (the opposite sense).
usage.zh: 作谓语；贬义很重。不要与“置之死地而后生”混淆。

meaning.en: To flatter someone with lavish praise.
meaning.zh: 给人说好听的奉承话。

examples.zh: 他最爱给领导戴高帽子。
examples.en: He loves buttering up the boss.

examples.zh: 别给我戴高帽子，有话直说吧。
examples.en: Don't flatter me; just say what you want.

examples.zh: 她被人戴高帽子戴得晕头转向。
examples.en: She was so showered with flattery that she lost her bearings.

usage.en: Verb-object, separable (给某人戴高帽子); colloquial, derogatory.
usage.zh: 动宾结构，可拆开用（给某人戴高帽子）；口语，贬义。

natural: show oneself in an ugly light

meaning.en: To fully expose one's unsightly behaviour or true nature.
meaning.zh: 丑恶的样子完全暴露出来。

equivalents: show up in one's true colours

examples.zh: 几杯酒下肚，他丑态毕露。
examples.en: A few drinks in, he showed himself in an ugly light.

examples.zh: 在利益面前，这伙人丑态毕露。
examples.en: Faced with money, these people revealed their ugly side.

examples.zh: 他在镜头前丑态毕露，网友一片哗然。
examples.en: He made an ugly spectacle of himself on camera, and netizens were outraged.

usage.en: Predicate; derogatory; subject is usually a person or group.
usage.zh: 作谓语；贬义，主语多为人或团体。

pinyin: rén rén dé ér zhū zhī

meaning.en: So hateful that everybody has the right to punish him.
meaning.zh: 罪大恶极，人人都有权惩处他。

examples.zh: 这种出卖国家的叛徒，人人得而诛之。
examples.en: A traitor who sells out his country is one whom everyone may rightly punish.

examples.zh: 残害儿童的恶人，人人得而诛之。
examples.en: Whoever harms children is a villain whom all may condemn.

examples.zh: 贪官污吏，人人得而诛之。
examples.en: Corrupt officials are hated by all and deserve punishment.

usage.en: Predicate; formal, typically in a verdict of public opinion.
usage.zh: 作谓语；书面语，多表示公愤。

natural: like rain that only wets the surface

meaning.en: Doing something so perfunctorily that it only skims the surface and leaves no lasting effect.
meaning.zh: 像雨水只把地面浸湿一样，比喻做事流于表面，没有深入，效果不大。

examples.zh: 这次检查水过地皮湿，问题一个也没解决。
examples.en: The inspection only skimmed the surface and solved not one problem.

examples.zh: 培训班水过地皮湿，学员什么也没学到。
examples.en: The training course was a flash in the pan; trainees learned nothing.

examples.zh: 改革不能水过地皮湿，必须深入下去。
examples.en: Reform must not just skim the surface; it has to go deep.

usage.en: Predicate or complement, colloquial; criticises formalism.
usage.zh: 作谓语或补语，口语；批评形式主义。

meaning.en: Just arrived and not yet familiar with the place or people.
meaning.zh: 刚刚来到一个地方，对环境和人都不熟悉。

examples.zh: 我初来乍到，还请大家多多关照。
examples.en: I'm new here, so please look after me.

examples.zh: 初来乍到的新同学总有点拘束。
examples.en: New classmates are always a little shy.

examples.zh: 他新来乍到，连路都找不着。
examples.en: He's only just arrived and can't even find his way.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; often used in self-introduction or an apology for ignorance.
usage.zh: 作谓语或定语；常用于自我介绍或表示不熟悉。

meaning.en: A handful of earth: a grave, or the last resting place.
meaning.zh: 一捧黄土，指坟墓，或人死后的归宿。

examples.zh: 英雄一生功业，最后只剩一抔黄土。
examples.en: A hero's lifetime of deeds ends as a handful of earth.

examples.zh: 多少帝王将相，终归一抔黄土。
examples.en: How many emperors and generals have all ended as a handful of earth.

examples.zh: 老人只愿落叶归根，求一抔黄土安身。
examples.en: The old man only wished to return home and rest under a handful of earth.

usage.en: Noun phrase; literary, often reflecting on mortality.
usage.zh: 名词性短语；书面语，常用于感叹人生无常。

meaning.en: Very costly, at an expense that is hard to measure.
meaning.zh: 花费极大，难以计量。

examples.zh: 这座大桥规模宏大，所费不赀。
examples.en: The bridge is huge and cost a fortune.

examples.zh: 为了修复古建筑，政府所费不赀。
examples.en: The government has spent enormous sums restoring the old building.

examples.zh: 这次婚礼办得排场十足，所费不赀。
examples.en: The wedding was lavish and cost a great deal.

usage.en: Predicate; formal. Often miswritten 所费不菲 / 所费不资; 赀 is read zī.
usage.zh: 作谓语；书面语。常被误写成“所费不菲”“所费不资”，“赀”读zī。

meaning.en: Describing a great body of water, vast and rushing.
meaning.zh: 形容水势浩大、奔腾不息。

examples.zh: 长江浩浩汤汤，奔流入海。
examples.en: The Yangtze, vast and surging, rushes to the sea.

examples.zh: 洪水浩浩汤汤，淹没了大片农田。
examples.en: The flood, mighty and rolling, drowned broad fields.

examples.zh: 浩浩汤汤的黄河，哺育了中华文明。
examples.en: The vast, rolling Yellow River nourished Chinese civilisation.

story.en: Fan Zhongyan describes Lake Dongting: 'Vast and rushing, boundless in breadth' (浩浩汤汤，横无际涯).
story.zh: 范仲淹《岳阳楼记》：“衔远山，吞长江，浩浩汤汤，横无际涯。”

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; 汤 reads shāng here, not tāng. Differs from 浩浩荡荡 (which is also used for processions).
usage.zh: 作谓语或定语；“汤”读shāng。与“浩浩荡荡”不同，后者也可形容队伍声势。

literal: guess · fist · carry out · drinking command

meaning.en: To play finger-guessing and other drinking games at a feast.
meaning.zh: 宴席上划拳、行酒令，热闹喝酒。

examples.zh: 酒席上大家猜拳行令，热闹非凡。
examples.en: At the banquet everybody played drinking games, and it was lively.

examples.zh: 隔壁包间里传来猜拳行令的声音。
examples.en: Sounds of finger games and drinking forfeits came from the next private room.

examples.zh: 他们猜拳行令，一直喝到深夜。
examples.en: They played drinking games and kept drinking until late at night.

usage.en: Predicate; casual, describing noisy drinking parties.
usage.zh: 作谓语；口语，描述喧闹的酒席。

meaning.en: Of some modest help; better than nothing.
meaning.zh: 不是完全没有益处，多少有点帮助。

examples.zh: 这笔钱虽然不多，对灾区也不无小补。
examples.en: The sum is small, but it helps the disaster area a little.

examples.zh: 每天读半小时，对提高语感不无小补。
examples.en: Reading half an hour a day does help your feel for language somewhat.

examples.zh: 多一个人帮忙，也不无小补。
examples.en: One more helper is of some use.

usage.en: Predicate; understated, formal; implies the help is limited.
usage.zh: 作谓语；语气委婉、书面，暗示帮助有限。

text: 智者不惑，仁者不忧，勇者不惧
pinyin: zhì zhě bù huò, rén zhě bù yōu, yǒng zhě bù jù
literal: wise one · not · confused · humane one · not · worried · brave one · not · afraid
natural: the wise are not perplexed, the humane not anxious, the brave not afraid

meaning.en: The wise are free from doubt, the benevolent from worry, the brave from fear.
meaning.zh: 有智慧的人不迷惑，仁德的人不忧愁，勇敢的人不畏惧。

equivalents: the wise, the good and the brave

examples.zh: “智者不惑，仁者不忧，勇者不惧”，这是儒家理想人格的写照。
examples.en: 'The wise are not perplexed, the humane not anxious, the brave not afraid': this portrays the Confucian ideal of character.

examples.zh: 校训取自“智者不惑，仁者不忧，勇者不惧”。
examples.en: The school motto comes from 'the wise are not perplexed, the humane not anxious, the brave not afraid'.

examples.zh: 他一生坦荡，真可谓智者不惑，仁者不忧，勇者不惧。
examples.en: He lived an open-hearted life: truly wise without doubt, humane without worry, brave without fear.

story.en: Confucius said: 'The wise are not perplexed, the humane do not worry, the brave are not afraid' (知者不惑，仁者不忧，勇者不惧).
story.zh: 《论语·子罕》：“子曰：知者不惑，仁者不忧，勇者不惧。”

usage.en: Quotation (Analects 子罕, written 知者); used in mottos and speeches.
usage.zh: 名言（《论语·子罕》作“知者不惑”），常用于校训、演讲。

text: 天下本无事，庸人自扰之
pinyin: tiān xià běn wú shì, yōng rén zì rǎo zhī
literal: the world · originally · no · trouble · mediocre person · himself · stirs up · it
natural: there was no trouble until fools stirred it up

meaning.en: The world is basically at peace; foolish people create their own trouble.
meaning.zh: 天下原本没有什么事，是庸俗的人自己惹出麻烦。

examples.zh: 天下本无事，庸人自扰之，你不必这样焦虑。
examples.en: The world is quiet until fools stir it up, so there is no need to be this anxious.

examples.zh: 两家本无矛盾，是传言惹祸，天下本无事，庸人自扰之。
examples.en: The two families had no quarrel; rumours caused it. There was no trouble until people made it.

examples.zh: 别疑神疑鬼了，天下本无事，庸人自扰之。
examples.en: Stop imagining things: there was no trouble until you made some.

story.en: Lu Xiangxian said that the world was basically at peace and only mediocre officials made trouble by their fuss (天下本无事，庸人扰之为烦耳).
story.zh: 陆象先说：“天下本无事，庸人扰之为烦耳。”

usage.en: Proverb; the original reads 庸人扰之, the common modern form adds 自.
usage.zh: 谚语；原文作“庸人扰之为烦耳”，今多作“庸人自扰之”。

pinyin: chuī miàn bù hán yáng liǔ fēng
literal: blow · face · not · cold · willow · wind
natural: the willow breeze on the face is not cold

meaning.en: The gentle spring breeze among the willows does not chill the face.
meaning.zh: 春风拂面，带着杨柳的气息，一点也不觉得寒冷。

examples.zh: 走在河堤上，吹面不寒杨柳风，让人心旷神怡。
examples.en: Walking along the embankment, the soft willow breeze on my face made my spirits lift.

examples.zh: “沾衣欲湿杏花雨，吹面不寒杨柳风”写尽了春天的温柔。
examples.en: 'Apricot rain wets the sleeve, willow breeze doesn't chill the face' captures the gentleness of spring.

examples.zh: 三月的清晨，吹面不寒杨柳风。
examples.en: On a March morning, the willow breeze is no longer cold on the face.

story.en: The monk Zhi Nan's quatrain: 'Apricot rain about to wet my clothes, willow breeze that does not chill my face' (沾衣欲湿杏花雨，吹面不寒杨柳风).
story.zh: 南宋僧人志南《绝句》：“古木阴中系短篷，杖藜扶我过桥东。沾衣欲湿杏花雨，吹面不寒杨柳风。”

usage.en: Poetic line used to describe spring weather; often paired with 沾衣欲湿杏花雨.
usage.zh: 诗句，用于描写春天的天气，常与“沾衣欲湿杏花雨”对举。

pinyin: shàng zhī tiān wén xià zhī dì lǐ
literal: above · know · astronomy · below · know · geography
natural: know astronomy above and geography below

meaning.en: To be extremely learned, knowing about everything under the sun.
meaning.zh: 形容知识渊博，什么都知道。

examples.zh: 他上知天文下知地理，什么话题都能聊。
examples.en: He knows heaven above and earth below, and can talk about any topic.

examples.zh: 别以为自己上知天文下知地理，其实还有很多不懂。
examples.en: Don't think you know everything from astronomy to geography; there is still much you don't understand.

examples.zh: 爷爷读书多，被邻居称为上知天文下知地理。
examples.en: Grandfather has read widely, and the neighbours say he knows everything from the stars to the earth.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; colloquial praise, often jokey or exaggerated.
usage.zh: 作谓语或定语；口语，多含夸张或调侃。
